name: classaction-v1
description: Evaluation dataset for the Facebook/Meta Consumer Privacy class action settlement (Case No. 3:18-MD-02843-VC). Questions and gold passages drawn from 3 court documents: Final Approval Order, Plan of Allocation, and Claim Form.

questions.question: What is the total settlement amount?

gold_passages.text: The $725 million Settlement provides substantial benefits for the Class in light of the strengths and weaknesses of the claims asserted.

expected_answer.answer_text: The total settlement amount is $725 million.

questions.question: Is the settlement fund reversionary?

gold_passages.text: This is a common fund settlement; there shall be no reversion of the Settlement Fund to Meta upon the occurrence of the Effective Date.

expected_answer.answer_text: No, this is a nonreversionary common fund settlement. There shall be no reversion of the Settlement Fund to Meta upon the occurrence of the Effective Date.

questions.question: Was the settlement reached through mediation?

gold_passages.text: the Court is aware, based on communications with mediator Jay Gandhi, that his involvement was critical in brokering a fair settlement. In addition, District Judge Jacqueline Scott Corley, who previously presided over discovery disputes in this matter, was involved in brokering the settlement.

expected_answer.answer_text: Yes, the settlement was reached through mediation with mediator Jay Gandhi and District Judge Jacqueline Scott Corley.

questions.question: Who is eligible for this class action settlement?

gold_passages.text: All Facebook users in the United States between May 24, 2007, and December 22, 2022, inclusive.
The Settlement Class includes the following: All Facebook users in the United States between May 24, 2007 and December 22, 2022.

expected_answer.answer_text: All Facebook users in the United States between May 24, 2007, and December 22, 2022, inclusive.

questions.question: What are the exclusions from the settlement class?

gold_passages.text: Excluded from the Settlement Class are (i) Meta and its employees, alleged co-conspirators, officers, directors, legal representatives, heirs, successors, and wholly or partly owned subsidiaries or affiliated companies; (ii) counsel for any plaintiff whose case was consolidated into this MDL and their employees, including but not limited to the undersigned counsel for Plaintiffs and the undersigned counsel's employees; (iii) individuals who submitted timely and valid exclusion requests

expected_answer.answer_text: Excluded from the Settlement Class are: (i) Meta and its employees, officers, directors, legal representatives, heirs, successors, and affiliated companies; (ii) counsel for plaintiffs and their employees; (iii) individuals who submitted valid exclusion requests; (iv) the Discovery Mediators, Special Master, and Settlement Mediator; and (v) the Judges and Court staff assigned to the case.

questions.question: Can non-natural persons like companies file claims?

gold_passages.text: Only natural persons can create Facebook accounts, and accordingly only natural persons who set up accounts can file claims. The Class definition is therefore clear about whether it includes non-natural persons.

expected_answer.answer_text: No, only natural persons can file claims. The court ruled that since only natural persons can create Facebook accounts, only natural persons who set up accounts can file claims.

questions.question: Who is the defendant in this case?

gold_passages.text: Defendant Facebook, Inc., now known as Meta Platforms, Inc. ("Meta")

expected_answer.answer_text: The defendant is Facebook, Inc., now known as Meta Platforms, Inc. (Meta).

questions.question: Who are the settlement class representatives?

gold_passages.text: Plaintiffs Steven Akins, Jason Ariciu, Anthony Bell, Bridgett Burk, Terry Fischer, Tyler King, Jordan O'Hara, and Cheryl Senko (together, "Settlement Class Representatives")

expected_answer.answer_text: The Settlement Class Representatives are Steven Akins, Jason Ariciu, Anthony Bell, Bridgett Burk, Terry Fischer, Tyler King, Jordan O'Hara, and Cheryl Senko.

questions.question: Who is the settlement administrator?

gold_passages.text: The Court confirms its earlier appointment of Angeion Group to serve as the Settlement Administrator and finds that it thus far has fulfilled its duties under the Settlement.

expected_answer.answer_text: The settlement administrator is Angeion Group.

questions.question: What is the deadline to submit a claim?

gold_passages.text: Your Claim Form must be submitted by August 25, 2023. If you submit your claim by U.S. mail, make sure the completed and signed Claim Form is postmarked by August 25, 2023.

expected_answer.answer_text: The deadline to submit a claim is August 25, 2023. Claims can be submitted online by 11:59 p.m. PDT or by U.S. mail postmarked by August 25, 2023.

questions.question: When is the opt-out deadline?

gold_passages.text: Deadline for opt-outs July 26, 2023

expected_answer.answer_text: The opt-out deadline is July 26, 2023. Opt-out forms must be postmarked by July 26, 2023, or submitted electronically by 11:59 p.m. PDT on July 26, 2023.

questions.question: When was the final approval hearing held?

gold_passages.text: the Court held a Final Approval Hearing on September 7, 2023, to consider approval of this Settlement

expected_answer.answer_text: The Final Approval Hearing was held on September 7, 2023.

questions.question: How is the claim amount calculated for each class member?

gold_passages.text: The Net Settlement Fund—including, to the greatest extent practicable, all interest earned on the Settlement Fund—shall be allocated to each Authorized Claimant pro rata by reference to the total number of allocation points assigned to all Authorized Claimants.

For each calendar month at any time during which an Authorized Claimant was a Facebook user with an activated account during the Class Period, such Authorized Claimant shall be assigned one allocation point.

expected_answer.answer_text: The claim amount is calculated using allocation points distributed pro rata. Each Authorized Claimant receives one allocation point for each calendar month they had an activated Facebook account during the Class Period. The Net Settlement Fund is then divided proportionally based on total allocation points.

questions.question: Why is time on the platform used as the basis for calculating payments?

gold_passages.text: Meta has confirmed that there is a positive correlation between the length of time users have been on the platform and the degree to which third parties had access to users' information. Thus, the Plan of Allocation is designed to roughly track the probable extent to which third parties had access to Class Members' private information

expected_answer.answer_text: Meta confirmed a positive correlation between length of time on the platform and the degree of third-party access to user information. The allocation method tracks the probable extent of third-party access to each class member's private information.

questions.question: Is there a minimum payment amount?

gold_passages.text: the Settlement Administrator shall have the discretion, after consulting with Class Counsel, to select an amount for minimum payments to Authorized Claimants, with the goal of ensuring that payments to Authorized Claimants are administratively and economically feasible and that as much of the Net Settlement Fund as possible is actually distributed to Authorized Claimants.

expected_answer.answer_text: The Settlement Administrator has discretion, after consulting with Class Counsel, to set a minimum payment amount. The goal is to ensure payments are administratively and economically feasible while distributing as much of the Net Settlement Fund as possible.

questions.question: What are the key dates in the settlement administration timeline?

gold_passages.text: Commencement of individual notice April 12, 2023 Completion of individual notice May 11, 2023 Deadline for objections July 26, 2023 Deadline for opt-outs July 26, 2023 Claims deadline August 25, 2023

expected_answer.answer_text: Key dates: notice commenced April 12, 2023; notice completed May 11, 2023; objections and opt-outs deadline July 26, 2023; claims deadline August 25, 2023; distribution commences 90 days after the Effective Date; substantial completion of distribution 165 days after the Effective Date.

questions.question: What payment methods are available for receiving settlement funds?

gold_passages.text: Prepaid Mastercard – Enter the email address where you will receive the Prepaid Mastercard

expected_answer.answer_text: Settlement payments can be received via Prepaid Mastercard, PayPal, Venmo, Zelle, or Physical Check.

questions.question: What happens to unclaimed settlement payments?

gold_passages.text: If a payment made according to sections 5-6 and distributed to an Authorized Claimant via a check is not negotiated within ninety (90) days after the Settlement Administrator has contacted, or made reasonable attempts to contact, the Authorized Claimant, the Authorized Claimant shall be deemed to have waived and released their claim for payment under the Settlement Agreement.

expected_answer.answer_text: Checks not negotiated within 90 days are forfeited and the claimant is deemed to have waived their claim. Undeliverable checks get one re-mailing attempt. If residual funds remain, Class Counsel and the Settlement Administrator propose an equitable redistribution to the Court.

questions.question: How many people were notified about the settlement?

gold_passages.text: more than 93% of the target audience of 253 million Americans had received notice, each with an average frequency of more than 3 times

expected_answer.answer_text: More than 93% of the target audience of 253 million Americans received notice, each with an average frequency of more than 3 times.
key_facts: average frequency of more than 3 times

questions.question: How much did Meta pay the FTC for the same conduct?

gold_passages.text: the $5 billion settlement paid by the company to the FTC for the conduct alleged in this case, and the fact that the company agreed to prospective relief with the FTC

expected_answer.answer_text: Meta paid a $5 billion settlement to the FTC for the same conduct alleged in this class action.

questions.question: What percentage of attorneys' fees is retained in the settlement fund?

gold_passages.text: Ten percent of Class Counsel's awarded attorneys' fees shall remain in the Settlement Fund until after Class Counsel files a Post-Distribution Accounting, as described herein, and the Court authorizes the release to Class Counsel of the attorneys' fees remaining in the Settlement Fund.

expected_answer.answer_text: Ten percent (10%) of Class Counsel's awarded attorneys' fees is retained in the Settlement Fund until after Class Counsel files a Post-Distribution Accounting.

questions.question: How can claims be submitted?

gold_passages.text: There are two ways to submit this Claim Form to the Settlement Administrator: (a) online at www.FacebookUserPrivacySettlement.com; or (b) by U.S. Mail to the following address: Facebook Consumer Privacy User Profile Litigation, c/o Settlement Administrator, 1650 Arch Street, Suite 2210, Philadelphia, PA 19103.

expected_answer.answer_text: Claims can be submitted online at www.FacebookUserPrivacySettlement.com or by U.S. Mail to Facebook Consumer Privacy User Profile Litigation, c/o Settlement Administrator, 1650 Arch Street, Suite 2210, Philadelphia, PA 19103.
